transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Lately I’ve been overwhelmed by guilt about letting everyone down at home and at work, even when people tell me it’s not that bad. It just feels like I'm failing everyone around me, and I can't seem to shake it.

Did these feelings start after a specific stressful event or major change in your life, or did they come on without a clear trigger? Also, have you been feeling more depressed, more anxious, or both about equally?

They really worsened during a stressful time at home with my teenage daughter pushing boundaries and my husband working long hours, combined with a hectic period at work. As for how I feel, it’s much more of a heavy, gray depression and overwhelming guilt rather than anxiety, though I do lie awake at night replaying arguments.

When you feel this guilt, does it ever seem so strong or fixed that you’re certain you’ve caused serious harm or deserve punishment, even when others say that isn’t true? Have you had any experiences like hearing accusatory voices or feeling convinced of things others say are not real?

I do feel a constant, heavy guilt that I'm a terrible mother and a lousy manager who is letting everyone down, even though my family and coworkers keep telling me I'm being too hard on myself. But I've never heard any voices, had hallucinations, or believed things that are completely out of touch with reality.

Because of these symptoms, have you become unable to keep up with basic daily responsibilities like going to work, taking care of yourself, or managing things at home? Or are you still functioning, even though it feels much harder?

I'm trying to force myself to keep going, but I'm failing to keep up and my team at work has had to quietly pick up my slack because I've been missing deadlines and forgetting meetings. Even basic chores like loading the dishwasher feel completely exhausting, and I keep backing out of plans with friends and family. It's gotten to the point where my daughter told me she doesn't even know which version of me she's coming home to anymore.

Have you had any thoughts that life isn’t worth living or that you’d be better off dead, or thoughts of harming yourself? Also, despite others reassuring you, do you ever feel absolutely certain that you deserve punishment or have ruined people’s lives?

No, I don’t have any thoughts of hurting myself or wanting to end my life. But I do feel constantly consumed by this overwhelming guilt, replaying my mistakes and feeling absolutely convinced that I'm a terrible mother and manager who has let everyone down, even though people tell me I'm being too hard on myself.
Have you also been feeling down or empty most of the day nearly every day, and have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy? If so, how long has that been going on?

Yes, most days I wake up with a heavy, gray feeling in my chest and feel on the verge of tears over minor things. I've also completely lost interest in my Saturday hikes and art classes, finding them flat and pointless. This current low stretch has been dragging on for about five months now.

Before this current 5-month period, have you ever had another episode lasting at least two weeks when you felt similarly depressed and lost interest in things? If so, did you return to your usual self in between episodes?

Yes, looking back, I've had similar low, drained periods lasting weeks or longer on and off for at least a few years before this current stretch. In between these cycles of feeling really high and then sinking low, I do generally return to my usual, steady self.

When you mentioned feeling “really high” between low periods, did you have times lasting several days when you needed much less sleep and felt unusually energetic, confident, or talkative, with racing thoughts or risky behavior? Or did “high” just mean feeling back to your normal self?

Yes, it was definitely much more than normal; I'd have stretches of a few weeks where I felt incredibly energized, sleeping only about four hours a night but waking up completely wired. During those times, my thoughts raced so fast that I'd talk over people, and I felt unusually confident—like I was the only one who could fix things at work—which led me to impulsively take on way too many projects and commitments.

final_diagnosis.reason: Current presentation is a depressive episode lasting about 5 months with depressed mood, marked anhedonia, guilt, insomnia, and clear functional impairment. History also confirms prior periods of elevated mood lasting weeks with decreased need for sleep, increased energy, pressured/talkative behavior, racing thoughts, inflated confidence, and impulsive overcommitment, consistent with hypomanic/manic-spectrum episodes. No hallucinations or bizarre delusions were reported, so bipolar affective disorder, current episode mild or moderate depression without psychotic symptoms is the best fit among the provided candidates.
